picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 lists single-agent PARP maintenance after a 1L platinum response as a category 2A option for all-comers, and PRIMA enrolled without requiring a BRCA mutation or a validated HRD score. That all-comer footing is what a BRCA wild-type, genomically unstable tumor needs, and the regimen is oral, which suits the patient's stated preference. ESMO endorses 1L PARP maintenance in this setting as well, so the cross-society read is consistent. The honest cost is myelosuppression, which sits on her toxicity veto list, though the individualized starting dose in PRIMA cut the grade 3+ thrombocytopenia rate.
primary_concerns: Triggers her severe-myelosuppression veto: grade 3+ thrombocytopenia 28.7% and anemia 31% in PRIMA, needing platelet-based starting dose and close counts
Guideline benefit is largest in the HRD-positive stratum; in the BRCA wild-type, HRD-unquantified setting the all-comer estimate is the relevant one and it is smaller

picks.rationale: PAOLA-1 is the category 1 NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 maintenance option for HRD-positive disease and carries an ESMO-MCBS score, so on guideline grounds this is the highest-tier choice if she qualifies. The catch is the gate: NCCN ties the indication to HRD-positive status defined by tumor BRCA or a validated GIS at or above 42, and Altera's qualitative instability call does not meet that companion-diagnostic bar. She is already on the bevacizumab backbone, which makes the add-on operationally clean. I rank it second only because eligibility hinges on a MyChoice CDx score she does not yet have; send the assay and the rank reorders if it comes back at 42 or higher.
primary_concerns: Off the guideline-endorsed population until a validated GIS confirms HRD-positive; below 42 she defaults to all-comer niraparib
Bevacizumab VTE and bleeding risk is live given her high VTE history and prior IVC filter; combination-arm grade 3+ hypertension was 19%

picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 lists bevacizumab maintenance as a category 2A all-comer option after 1L platinum, anchored by GOG-218 and ICON7, and she is already receiving it. ICON7 puts the largest gain in the high-risk subset, and a stage IIIc R0 patient sits adjacent to that group. Continuing it costs nothing in new decision-making and keeps a guideline-backed axis running while the GIS result decides whether olaparib gets layered on. The benefit is PFS, not OS, in the overall population, so I would not oversell it.
primary_concerns: VTE, bleeding, and hypertension class risk is the operative caution given her VTE history and IVC filter, even though no neuropathy or myelosuppression veto is triggered
Overall-population benefit is PFS-only; OS was not improved in GOG-218 and the ICON7 OS gain was confined to the high-risk subset

picks.rationale: ATHENA-MONO supports rucaparib as another all-comer 1L PARP maintenance option, with benefit holding in the intent-to-treat population that includes the BRCA wild-type stratum, so she qualifies without a BRCA gate. NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 carries the same single-agent PARP maintenance category 2A recommendation that covers this agent. I place it below niraparib mainly on label and prescribing familiarity in the 1L all-comer setting rather than any efficacy gap. Her baseline LFTs are normal, which helps with rucaparib's transaminase signal.
primary_concerns: Same severe-myelosuppression veto applies: grade 3+ anemia 28.7% and neutropenia 14.6%
Effect size confirmed as the primary JCO ITT HR 0.52 (pmid 35658487)

picks.rationale: NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 includes aromatase inhibitors among hormone-therapy options for recurrent or maintenance ER-positive disease, and her tumor is ER-positive in roughly 80% of nuclei. Letrozole is oral and low-burden, which fits her age band and preference, and none of her toxicity vetoes apply. PR-negativity predicts a tempered response, and the supporting evidence here is a non-randomized retrospective comparison rather than a randomized trial, so I rank it as a low-toxicity later-line or adjunct option rather than the primary maintenance choice. The guideline category for endocrine therapy is softer than the 2A PARP and bevacizumab recommendations above.
primary_concerns: ER-positive but PR-negative, which tempers the expected endocrine magnitude
Supporting data are retrospective and non-randomized (ROBINS-I serious), a weaker evidence base than the PARP and bevacizumab options

notes: Ranking is anchored to NCCN Ovarian v1.2025 categories. The cleanest guideline fit is all-comer 1L PARP maintenance (niraparib, PRIMA), which needs neither a BRCA mutation nor a validated HRD score, so it carries no contingency for this BRCA wild-type tumor. PAOLA-1 is the higher-tier category 1 regimen but is gated on a validated GIS the Altera qualitative call does not provide; the shared rank-1 workup the board should agree on is sending a MyChoice CDx (or FDA-equivalent) score, since a result at or above 42 promotes olaparib + bevacizumab over niraparib. SOLO1 (olaparib monotherapy) is foreclosed by BRCA wild-type status and is not ranked. GEN-1/IMNN-001 is the on-study investigational regimen she received and matters for board context, but it is not guideline-endorsed maintenance, so I leave it off the ranked list. The PIK3CA and MAP2K4 baskets are investigational-only with no approved matched therapy and no guideline standing; off-list for this persona.
